text:
maria: Heads up — canary on chat.prod shows a p95 spike right after the kernel switchover :eyes:
aj: saw that alert this morning, details?
liam: I'm on it. quick summary from the canary dashboard: p50 ~ 40ms stable, p95 jumped from ~190ms -> 420ms at 09:12 UTC when kernel v2.14 landed.
maria: KV cache hit rate also dropped around the same time: before 78% -> after 52%. suspecting eviction pattern change + microbatching interaction.
nina: any evidence batch sizes changed?
liam: yes, sample from trace shows a bunch of single-request microbatches. prefetched KV misses caused longer generation paths. snippet from profiler:
```
# recent samples
batch_size_hist: {1: 63%, 2: 18%, 4+: 19%}
kv_cache_hits: 52.3%
latency_p95_ms: 422
kernel_version: v2.14
```
aj: that batch_size_hist is worrying — continuous batching heuristics should avoid so many singletons.
maria: my quick hypothesis: kernel v2.14 changed attention kernel memory layout so KV slice alignment differs -> more cache churn -> requests not hitting shared prefix caches -> batcher sees smaller effective batch aggregation window.
liam: ran a micro repro on canary with high-qps synthetic workload. reproduces p95 bump only when route token_target < 100 and kv hit < 60%.
nina: can we tweak token budget targets per route tier as a stopgap? increase reserved tokens so longer-prefetch/KV-friendly batches form.
aj: propose quick canary patch: bump token_target for chat.prod and chat.tierA by +60 tokens, add hysteresis on queue wait (200ms) to allow one extra request to join.
maria: sounds reasonable. config diff suggestion:
```
route_token_targets:
  chat.prod: 220
  chat.tierA: 160
  chat.tierB: 90
batcher:
  max_queue_wait_ms: 200
  queue_hysteresis_ms: 100
```
liam: will that increase latency tail for tiny requests? risk of slightly higher p50 for tiny requests, but should reduce p95.
nina: acceptable trade for canary until we fully root cause. can we also pin kernel back on canary while we test token diff?
maria: yes pls pin kernel v2.13 on 20% of canary fleet and rollout token change to other 80% so we can A/B.
perf-bot: canary job started: test-run id=ci-37765432; monitoring hooks enabled.
aj: I'll push token-target patch to canary now.
liam: I'm running the prefetched-KV profiler against both kernel variants, enabling --trace-kv-hotness.
maria: action items: aj deploy token patch, liam gather traces and KV heatmaps, nina coord with console to watch per-route p95 and KV hit.
nina: noted, I'll set alerts for kv_hit < 60% and p95 > 300ms on chat.prod.
liam: preliminary after 10m: p95 on patched canary dropped to ~205ms, kv_hit up to 69% on patched instances, pinned-kernel instances still at 410ms and kv_hit 51%.
maria: looks promising. we should still schedule deeper kernel-root cause with infra + runtime team next week.
aj: rolling token patch to 100% if no regressions in next 30m. I'll hold if liam sees anything odd in traces.
liam: will post full trace dump and a short notebook with KV hotness maps in the thread when ready.
maria: thanks all. small wins but need follow-up RFC for kernel+batcher contract and explicit KV alignment tests in CI. :white_check_mark:
